newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Twenty-four carat gold closed 25 rupees lower at 4,525 rupees per 10 grammes on Monday due to light profit-taking, dealers said.
Sluggish physical demand, despite approaching festivals, also subdued market sentiment. However, traders are expecting higher festival-related buying next month.
"Gold prices may bounce back in the coming days," one broker said.
The price of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed 300 rupees lower at 52,900 per piece after gaining 300 rupees on Saturday.

Silver (.999) closed 35 rupees higher at 6,330 rupees per kg as fresh industrial buying dragged prices upward, while supplies remained at a low ebb during the day. Silver was up 45 rupees per kg on Saturday.
An uptrend in the world market kept sentiment towards the silver market firm at the close of the session.
